title: Bridging Balancing Weights and Augmentation in Covariate-adjusted Analyses with Time-to-Event Endpoints: Theory and Practical Recommendations
summary: Covariate adjustment improves the efficiency of treatment-effect analyses in randomized clinical trials, provided the adjustment targets the correct quantity. For time-to-event endpoints, two marginal targets are of primary interest: the log-rank test for the presence of a treatment effect and the marginal hazard ratio for its magnitude. Existing covariate adjustment approaches reach these targets by different ways. Augmentation adjusts the log-rank score by regressing derived outcomes on the baseline covariates within each arm.
